search_window.basis: Start is completed_at of latest verified preceding Food Line Source Watch heartbeat on ops/watch-ledger; end is Pacific local execution time after bounded search. Publication and indexing recency alone do not establish a new event.

coverage_notes: Supplementary recall watch, not the primary collector; no primary Food Line production collection was accessed or modified.

Twelve targeted fast web searches completed across all four miss classes, with two-day recency requested. The search provider returned substantial older material, so actual source publication dates and disruption time were not inferred from crawl recency.

No newly published and independently substantiated qualifying food-access disruption or official benefit interruption was found in the 2026-10-26 22:52:22 to 2026-10-26T23:46:55-07:00 Pacific observation interval. Absence of verified findings is not proof of absence of incidents.

Results for only/last/full-service grocery closures were older (for example, Eastport Maine in August 2026; Avondale Cincinnati summer 2026; North Charleston August 2026) and excluded as out of window.

Distribution and pantry searches returned older articles such as the March 2026 Columbus Georgia cancellation and a September 2026 Palm Springs Saturday food bank suspension, not new qualifying notices.
Official SNAP/WIC/outage searches largely surfaced October–November 2025 government-shutdown benefit stories rather than a new October 26, 2026 official disruption; these were excluded.
No search-level failure identified, but narrow query matching, publisher indexing lag, unindexed provider channels, and limited local-news reach remain coverage limitations.
No editorial approval, publication, schedule update, task disabling, or other operational change occurred.
